text:
aina: quick take 1: can we avoid a full runtime compat shim? propose a lightweight gateway shim that only translates a small set of headers and unwraps legacy envelopes. much lower risk than touching the runtime.

sam: curious about scope. which fields are in/out of scope? if we only do headers + envelope, some client-side errors might be invisible to downstream services. :thinking:
maria: telemetry answer: add a shim.trace header and emit mapped_field.{name}.drop and mapped_field.{name}.null counters. if we see any spike >0.2% per 24h we alert.

aina: lifecycle we thought of: 1) opt-in via X-RI-Compat: 1 2) run shim only for opt-ins 3) after 30d of stable metrics, flip selected tenants to opt-out (behind FF) 4) schedule retirement at 90d after majority opt-out. prevents indefinite support.
tom: perf note 1: avoid full JSON.parse for every req. shim should be lazy: parse only if header present or tenant flagged. set a 15ms transform budget and a circuit-breaker to bypass shim if exceeded.

sam: SDK ergonomics: older SDKs sometimes don't let customers add headers easily. we should ship tiny adapter snippets for each SDK and a console toggle for tenant-level opt-ins.

leo: ops: add a `shim.bypass_count` metric and a histogram for transform_latency_ms. also add a label shim.version so we can roll forward.

devops-bot: deployed gateway-compat v0.1 to canary (prod-us-east-1) - traffic 1% - logs at /infra/gateway/compat/2026-03-23/

aina: sample gateway config (implementation sketch):

```
mappings:
  - id: legacy-envelope
    trigger_header: X-RI-Compat
    translate_headers:
      "Legacy-Client-Ver": "X-Client-Version"
    body_unwrap: true
    timeout_ms: 15
    circuit_breaker: "window_ms=3000;max_latency_ms=20"
```

maria: I'll add tracing tags: shim.used=true, shim.version, shim.mapped_fields_count, shim.mapped_field_errors. alerts: page on error_rate > 0.5% for 6h.

aina: action items: sam -> SDK snippets + console opt-in UX; maria -> metrics + alerts; tom -> perf guard + cb; leo -> rollout runbook; jen (cc) -> migration playbook for CS. reconvene in 1 week to review canary metrics. :thumbsup:
